## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**System Name:** Main House  
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
**CRITICAL ISSUE IDENTIFIED.** The effluent pump is operating at no load. The pump motor is running but delivering no hydraulic output. This condition poses immediate risk of motor damage from overheating. Immediate professional attention is required.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The combined solids layer (scum plus sludge) measures 11 inches in a 48-inch fluid depth, placing the system within normal operating range. The effluent filter was clean and lightly soiled at the time of service.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Measurement | Value | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Measured Amp Draw | 1.6 A | CRITICAL |
| Nameplate Rating | 7.2 A | -- |
| Load Percentage | 22.2% FLA | CRITICAL - No Load |

The pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated amperage. This indicates the pump motor is operating without hydraulic load -- the impeller is either not turning, broken, or missing, or the discharge line is severed or disconnected. A pump running dry will overheat rapidly and fail. The high water alarm tested functional, and electrical connections are sound.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (CRITICAL):**
- Immediate professional attention is required to diagnose and repair the effluent pump. The pump must be examined to determine whether the impeller is broken or missing, or whether the discharge line is severed or disconnected. Do not operate the system further until the pump is repaired or replaced. Continued operation risks catastrophic motor failure.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once pump operation is restored and verified.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

Your system is an aerobic treatment unit that relies on the effluent pump to move treated water from the tank to the dispersal field. During this maintenance visit, the pump was found to be running but delivering no flow. This is a critical fault that must be corrected immediately.

The tank itself is in good condition. Solids are accumulating at a normal rate. Once the pump is repaired, the system can resume normal operation.

Do not delay in calling a qualified technician to examine and repair the pump. Running the system with a failed pump will cause the tank to back up and can damage the treatment unit.
